identity.name: Frisia
alt_names: Frisian lands east of the Lauwers

land.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers, 33 cells, the same outline Cliopatria gives the 'Frisians' row in 793-799

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Magna Frisia (the 'Frisian Kingdom') ends in 771 and this row begins in 783; the pages opened date no break. The Frisian Realm itself ended in 734 (Frisia page).

land.text: 'the area east of the Lauwers', conquered by Frankish troops in 785

successors.note: Cliopatria's Frankish shape does not cover the land until 788 (my gazetteer check: no overlap in 783-787, all 49 cells from 788).

correction.text: the land east of the Lauwers only, 783-785, instead of Cliopatria's 49-cell shape that adds Friesland west of the Lauwers and runs to 787

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 12,911 km2 (49 cells, 5.2 to 8.5 E) for 783-787 is too large and too long. Gazetteer check (mine): 33 of its cells are the land east of the Lauwers (identical to Cliopatria's Magna Frisia 741-771 and 'Frisians' 793-799 outline), the other 16 are Friesland west of the Lauwers, which the Frisia page has under the Franks since the Frisian Realm ended in 734 'at the Battle of the Boarn, when the Frisians were defeated by the Franks'. 'Frankish troops conquered the area east of the Lauwers in 785, after Charlemagne defeated the Saxon leader Widukind', so the free Frisia ends in 785, not 787. Infobox areas of the page are modern ('narrow sense' 9,378.7 km2, 'broad sense' 13,482.7 km2): the Cliopatria shape matches the broad one (ratio 0.96) and the corrected shape (8,793 km2) the narrow one (0.94), neither a check on the 8th century.

region.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers

ledger.note: 783: Cliopatria's Frisia row begins. The pages date no founding: the Frisia page ends the Frisian Realm (650-734) 'in 734 at the Battle of the Boarn' and gives no break between 734 and the 785 Frankish conquest of the land east of the Lauwers. Confidence 1: the year is Cliopatria's, the land is the Frisians' last free land.

region.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers, fought over 783-785

ledger.note: 783: the Saxon Wars reach their fiercest phase. 'The action led to two straight years of constant warfare (783-785), with Charlemagne wintering in central Saxony, at Minden'; the infobox lists 'Saxons; Frisians' among the belligerents. The page does not say where the fighting reached Frisia: the year is the page's, the zone is my reading.

region.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers

ledger.note: 785: the end of the fighting. 'Frankish troops conquered the area east of the Lauwers in 785, after Charlemagne defeated the Saxon leader Widukind' (Saxon Wars: 'The turning point came in 785, when Widukind was baptized and swore fealty to Charlemagne').

785: Frankish troops conquer the Frisian land east of the Lauwers: 'Frankish troops conquered the area east of the Lauwers in 785, after Charlemagne defeated the Saxon leader Widukind.' The page adds, undated, that 'The Carolingians laid Frisia under the rule of grewan' (a title 'loosely related to count').

region.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers

ledger.note: 785: free Frisia ends. The page's conquest year ends the state; Cliopatria keeps the row to 787 and its Frankish shape does not cover the land until 788 (keyframe verdict adjust). Cliopatria draws a 'Frisians' row on the same outline again in 793-799: no page opened explains it.

wars.name: Saxon Wars

zones.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers, conquered in 785

wars.outcome: Frankish victory: 'Frankish annexation of Saxony'; Widukind was baptized in 785 and the last rebellion was defeated in 804. The Frisian share: the land east of the Lauwers was conquered in 785.
wars.note: The Saxon Wars page lists 'Saxons; Frisians' as belligerents but says nothing else about Frisia and does not mention the Lauwers; the 785 Lauwers sentence is from the Frisia page. [Reviewer eu-07-c, 2026-10-24: clipped from the page's 772-804 to this dossier's life and the Frisian share, 'two straight years of constant warfare (783-785)' (Saxon Wars page).]

certainty.note: The Lauwers is a river line named by the page; the coast and the Saxon frontier in the south are approximate.

notes: Wikidata Q4492881 is shared with 'Frisia Kingdom' (frisia-kingdom, 612-717, group eu-06): they are different states in Cliopatria's data. That row's 63,720 km2 shape lies at 7.1-11.1 E, 46.9-50.5 N (south-west Germany, Switzerland, Alsace), nowhere near Frisia: the owner should check it. Cliopatria also draws the same land-east-of-the-Lauwers outline as 'Magna Frisia' (741-771, group eu-06) and 'Frisians' (793-799, group eu-07) and a larger 'Frisia' here (783-787); my reading, from the Frisia page, is one free Frisia east of the Lauwers ending in 785 and everything west of it Frankish since 734. The Frankish dossier should cover the land from 785, not 788. Not settled in two pages: why Cliopatria redraws the Frisians in 793-799 (a revolt would need a page), and the Frankish campaigns of 719-734 before this state's life (the Frisia page gives only the 734 Boarn). No capital: none on the pages for 783-785. No gazetteer names needed.
